candidates.title: BNSF hit by severe weather in Southwest and Nebraska
candidates.excerpt: BNSF Railway is continuing recovery after flooding at two locations on its system this week. On Thursday, Oct. 1, the railroad reported service disruptions in the Lincoln, Neb., area after 4 to 5 inches of rain fell in a few hours led to widespread flooding. High water disrupted operations at the railroad’s Lincoln Yard, with road closures in the region creating additional issues. BNSF’s customer advisory says shipments will experience delays and longer-than-normal transit times. BNSF also experienced a derailment about 4:30 p.m. on Thursday anear Pleasantville, Iowa, involving about 25 cars of a 57-car westbound train, KCCI-TV reports. No injuries were reported and no hazardous materials were involved. There is no initial word if the incident is weather related, but Pleasantville is about 25 miles southeast of Des Moines, which received more than an inch of rain in the 24 hours ending Thursday at 4 p.m. and had the third-wettest September in its history (14.5 inches of rain), accordin

candidates.title: Friends of East Broad Top raises $564,516, opens 2027 campaign
candidates.excerpt: SALTILLO, Pa. – Friends of the East Broad Top Railroad officers announced on Thursday, Oct. 1, that the group had raised a record $564,516 from 1,456 donors in its 2026 campaign, and kicked off an equally ambitious fundraising drive for 2027. The nonprofit organization is the all-volunteer auxiliary to the EBT Foundation, Inc., which owns the East Broad Top Railroad, a narrow-gauge heritage line in central Pennsylvania that is a National Historic Landmark. For its 2027 campaign, which began Thursday, the Friends set a goal of $375,000. The single largest chunk of that is earmarked for the two groups’ drive to continue to open 9 miles of main line – idled for 70 years – linking EBT headquarters at Rockhill Furnace, Pa., and the town of Saltillo. candidates.title: Hapag-Lloyd warns of Malaysia’s new manifest rule
candidates.excerpt: Hapag-Lloyd has advised customers that Malaysia’s “No Manifest, No Load” requirement now applies to export cargo with immediate effect. Under the rule introduced by the Royal Malaysian Customs Department, containers must have a valid and complete K5 export manifest before loading. Customers must submit complete and accurate Shipping Instructions at least 48 hours before the vessel’s estimated arrival at the Malaysian port of loading. For cargo transshipping through Malaysia, the information required for the K6 transshipment manifest must also be submitted at least 48 hours before the vessel’s arrival at the transshipment port. Containers with missing, incomplete or late Shipping Instructions may not appear on the approved manifest. As a result, port operators may refuse loading and roll the cargo to a later vessel. candidates.title: Maersk announces new PSS from South America to Europe
candidates.excerpt: Maersk will introduce and revise its Peak Season Surcharge on container shipments from the East Coast of South America to several European markets. The surcharge will apply from a Price Calculation Date of 1 November 2026. The charge applies to all dry and refrigerated container sizes covered by the announcement.

candidates.title: Interview with Ivan Jiménez, Port of Bilbao President: Reliability Is the New Competitive Advantage
candidates.excerpt: Reliability is becoming a key competitive factor for ports as global supply chains face growing uncertainty. That is the view of Ivan Jiménez, President of the Port of Bilbao, who sees resilience, connectivity and decarbonisation as central to the port’s long-term strategy. In the latest episode of CN Talks, Antonia Saratsopoulou, Managing Editor of Container News, spoke with Jiménez about Bilbao’s recent growth and future plans. The discussion covered container connectivity, rail development, port electrification and digitalisation. It also explored how Bilbao is preparing for geopolitical and climate-related disruption. According to Jiménez, the port has recorded its strongest start to a year in 22 years. Growth in liquid bulk traffic and containers has supported this performance. Container growth and greater diversification Higher liquid bulk volumes have been one of the drivers of Bilbao’s recent performance. candidates.title: Meratus Kutai makes first CIDX call at SP-ITC
candidates.excerpt: Meratus Kutai, the first vessel deployed on the new CIDX service, made its maiden call at SP-ITC Terminal in Ho Chi Minh City on 28 September 2026. The Meratus-operated service connects Vietnam with Indonesia, Timor-Leste and Papua New Guinea. Hai An Container Transport (HACT) acts as Meratus’ shipping agent in Vietnam. Representatives from SP-ITC welcomed the vessel’s crew and officials from Meratus and HACT during the call. SP-ITC presented its current operational capabilities and plans for further investment and expansion. These plans include the development of a deep-water port project in the Cai Mep area. Meanwhile, HACT outlined plans to expand its fleet and international network. The Vietnamese company also intends to develop additional domestic and international services calling at SP-ITC. The CIDX service provides a new maritime connection between Vietnam, Indonesia and markets across the Southwest Pacific.

candidates.title: Sea-Intelligence: August 2026 Reliability in Asia at 32.3%
candidates.excerpt: Figure 1 shows the country‑level vessel arrival schedule reliability for both July and August 2026, along with the Y/Y changes in each month. For nearly all countries, schedule reliability in August was lower than an already poor July, with the M/M declines ranging from ‑5.9 percentage points (pp) in Vietnam to ‑13.1 pp in South Korea. This shows that congestion is not a localised issue but is spread region‑wide. Thailand was the only country not to record a M/M decline in August, with its August 2026 figure 3.0 pp higher M/M. China was the most impacted in August, with the vessel schedule reliability in the country dropping to just 23.9%. Shanghai and Ningbo, which are the two largest ports in the country, saw their schedule reliability plummet to 12.2% and 16.9%, respectively.

candidates.title: ONE folds Hong Kong regional HQ into Singapore
candidates.excerpt: Ocean Network Express is consolidating its Asian regional management in Singapore, folding its Hong Kong-based East Asia headquarters into a new Asia Pacific operation from April 1, 2027. The Japanese containerline said the new Asia Pacific regional headquarters will combine its current East Asia operation in Hong Kong with the South Asia headquarters already based in Singapore. The enlarged unit will oversee 15 markets, with Louis Tang appointed regional head. ONE is also redrawing responsibility for Africa. Its East, West and South African businesses will move under the carrier’s Dubai regional headquarters, while London will retain responsibility for Europe, the Mediterranean and North Africa. The restructuring alters a regional setup that dates back to ONE’s creation. When NYK, MOL and K Line unveiled their merged container operation in 2017, Singapore was selected as global headquarters, with regional headquarters initially established in Hong Kong, London, Richmond and São Paulo.

candidates.title: Underwater stern tube seal replacement in under 48 hours in Algeciras
candidates.excerpt: Underwater stern tube seal replacement in under 48 hours in Algeciras Last month, a diver/technician team carried out an underwater stern tube seal replacement on a 180-meter container ship berthed in Algeciras. Seawater had been found in the air chamber and the seal leak alarm had gone off, confirming that the seals where damaged and needed to be replaced. Using a flexible mobdocks, the team was able to carry out the entire operation on-site and underwater, saving the owner an expensive and time-consuming trip to drydock. Once the operation was approved, all preparations were handled swiftly, and the required equipment was mobilized to the vessel. Because the ship’s mooring location could only be reached via the water, the team made use of a workboat during the operation. The operation started with the removal of the rope guard. candidates.title: Senators’ bill would provide pay raises for FRA inspectors
candidates.excerpt: WASHINGTON — Two U.S. senators have introduced a bill calling for increased pay for federal railroad inspectors, saying the Federal Railroad Administration has struggled to recruit and retain inspectors. Sens. Gary Peters (D-Mich.) and Jim Justice (R-W.Va) are sponsoring S. 5450, which would increase the pay classification for FRA inspectors by one level. This would boost maximum salaries for the jobs by nearly $20,000. “The United States railway system is critical to the success of our entire economy,” Peters said in a press release. “Federal railroad inspectors play a vital role in maintaining that system by ensuring railroad tracks, equipment, and operating practices remain safe and secure. candidates.excerpt: WASHINGTON — A Norfolk Southern conductor suffered serious injuries when he fell from the tank car he was riding during a shoving move, the National Transportation Safety Board says in its preliminary report on a Sept. 8, 2026, incident at Conway Yard in Conway, Pa. The report issued today (Oct. 1, 2026) addresses the latest of a series of serious injuries and fatalities that have occurred during shoving moves. The NTSB last month called for an end to crew members riding cars during switching shove moves, citing 14 deaths in such situations since October 2020 [see “NTSB recommends end …,” Trains.com, Sept. 21, 2026]. The injury occurred while the train’s crew was making a westbound move shoving a 219-car train from the main line into the yard. candidates.excerpt: WILKES-BARRE, Pa. — A deal is at hand to sell rail lines in Luzerne County, Pa., to the Reading & Northern Railroad following results of two board meetings this week. The R&N has offered $7 million for the lines currently owned by the Luzerne County Redevelopment Authority, and says it will spend another $3 million to upgrade the tracks to be able to handle excursion trains. The redevelopment agency accepted that offer on Tuesday, Sept. 29, and it was also accepted by the Luzerne County Council on Wednesday, Sept. 30, the Wilkes-Barre Citizens’ Voice reports. The redevelopment authority had initially accepted an $8.2 million offer from R.J. Corman Railroad Group, which currently operates 27 of the 60 miles of authority-owned trackage and right-of-way under a deal expiring Oct. 30. candidates.title: Judge rules that East Broad Top Foundation can buy Mount Union, Pa., property
candidates.excerpt: HUNTINGDON, Pa. — A Huntingdon County judge has ruled that the EBT Foundation can buy the East Broad Top Railroad’s Mount Union, Pa., dual-gauge yard and 4.7-mile stretch of main line. The segment was split from the rest of the railroad in 2013-2014, when the East Broad Top Preservation Association bought it from the Joseph Kovalchick family. That sale was the first step in what turned out to be a stillborn effort to restore the entire 33-mile narrow gauge line as a heritage railroad. The deal, approved by Judge Ray A. Ghaner, is subject to approval of the Pennsylvania attorney general’s office, as reported in a paywalled Altoona Mirror article. Ghaner ruled that a right of first refusal claimed by the Foundation was, in fact, valid and gave it two weeks in which to close the deal, which is worth $2 million. candidates.excerpt: Bathla collapse set to sharpen investor scrutiny of Australian private credit Investors in Australian private credit are expected to ask much tougher questions of their managers after the collapse of property developer Bathla Group. Centuria Bass paused redemptions and applications to two of its credit funds on 14 August, after a rise in redemption requests driven by concerns about Bathla. candidates.title: Another strong week for industrial rail freight
candidates.excerpt: U.S. weekly rail traffic totaled 537,397 carloads and intermodal units, up 4.85 compared with the same week a year ago, the Association of American Railroads (AAR) said. Traffic for the week ending September 26 totaled 235,787 carloads, up 3% compared with the same week in 2025, while intermodal volume of 301,610 containers and trailers was 6.3% higher compared to the same week in 2025. Seven of the 10 specific carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. They were led by metallic ores and metals, 9.5%; petroleum and related products, 9.4%; and chemicals, 7.2%. Shipments of farm products excluding grain and food fell by 3.3%, followed by coal, 2.1%, and motor vehicles and parts, 1.8%. Coal inventories are up 1.4 million tons since the end of 2025, while domestic consumption was down 11.4% y/y. candidates.excerpt: RCL books four more container ships at Huangpu-Wenchong The new contract expands RCL’s total boxship newbuilds at Huangpu Wenchong to 16 vessels CSSC Huangpu Wenchong Shipbuilding sealed a new construction contract with Thailand’s Regional Container Lines (RCL) for four units of its inhouse designed "Honghu" series 3,100 teu container ships. The signing took place on the same day that Huangpu Wenchong hosted a naming ceremony for three 4,488 teu container vessels built for RCL, with one of the ships delivered to the carrier on-site. This latest contract award brings RCL’s total container ship newbuilding portfolio at Huangpu Wenchong to 16 vessels, covering three distinct vessel types: eight 4,488 teu boxships, four 1,900 teu feeder vessels and the newly contracted four 3,100 teu "Honghu" units. candidates.excerpt: MSC container ship abandoned in South China Sea under tow Two tugs have joined the stricken container ship MSC Hermes III and all three vessels are headed to Vietnam The container ship MSC Hermes III abandoned in the South China Sea on 22 September would appear to be under tow to Vung Tau in Vietnam. The 20-year-old, 2,490 teu MSC Hermes III was reported to have sent a distress call at around 08:45 hrs SGT on 22 September and was rebroadcast by Singapore MRCC according to the Maritime & Port Authority of Singapore (MPA). The 25 crew of the vessel were reported to have abandoned ship into a lifeboat and were rescued by another MSC vessel MSC Ruby which answered the distress call. Two other MSC vessels MSC Florentina and the MSC Turin III also diverted to the vicinity of the MSC Hermes III that appeared to be adrift around 300 km east of Vietnam. The Annita Bhum, Benyapar Bhum, and Chantisa Bhum were named at the shipbuilders Longxue Yard in Guangzhou on 24 September. The naming ceremony was attended by RCL’s senior leadership, Dr. Jamlong Atikul, Chairman of the Board of Directors, Sumate Tanthuwanit, Chairman of the Executive Committee of RCL, and Dr. Twinchok Tanthuwanit, President of RCL, along with industry guests and stakeholders. The three newbuilds are the first in a series of eight container ships being built by RCL at CSSC Huangpu Wenchong Shipbuilding. Burglary hits moving BNSF train as container catches fire in Riverside
candidates.excerpt: A BNSF train carrying mixed freight caught fire during a burglary in Riverside, California, Thursday morning. The train was traveling from Los Angeles to Chicago, BNSF told FreightWaves. Firefighters found an open upper container burning on the moving double-stack train. Officials have not identified the items inside or reported any stolen cargo. Riverside dispatchers received the first report at 4:40 a.m. near Chicago Avenue. Early information placed the train heading west from downtown. Crews later located it moving east between Spruce and Columbia streets. Riverside Fire Department deployed 19 firefighters, four engines, one truck and a chief officer. Crews move train for access Access problems prevented crews from reaching the flames at their first location. Incident commanders directed railroad personnel to reposition the equipment farther east.
